instructions: Bring a medium pot of water to a boil. Add the vermicelli and cook it for 3 minutes, or as long as the package says. Drain it, rinse it under cold water and transfer it to a bowl.

Meanwhile, make the sauce off the heat. In a small bowl, whisk 3 tbsp peanut butter, 1 tbsp tamari, 2 tsp sugar, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 minced garlic clove and 1/3 cup of warm water until smooth. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more sugar.
Cut the tofu in half through its thickness, then into 1/2 inch strips, so each piece is about 3 inches long. Pat the strips dry with paper towels.

Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat for 1 minute. Add the tofu in a single layer and leave it alone for 3 minutes, until the underside is golden. Turn the strips and cook for 3 minutes.
Add 1 minced garlic clove, 1 tbsp tamari and 2 tsp sugar. Toss for 30 seconds, until the tofu is glazed and the pan is dry. Transfer it to a plate.
Cut the carrots and the cucumbers into thin matchsticks. Tear 12 lettuce leaves and cut out the thick cores. Pick 36 mint leaves off the stems.
Fill a wide shallow dish with warm water. Dip a rice paper sheet in for 2 seconds, then lay it flat on a cutting board. It will keep softening as you fill it.
Lay a lettuce leaf on the lower third of the sheet. Top it with a small handful of vermicelli, some carrot and cucumber, 2 or 3 pieces of tofu and 3 mint leaves.
Fold the bottom edge up over the filling, then fold in both sides. Roll it up firmly. Set it seam side down on a plate and make 11 more the same way.
Serve the rolls with the peanut sauce and the chili garlic sauce.
method_notes: Rice paper rolls are built the same way in every source: soft lettuce, vermicelli, herbs and vegetables rolled in a quickly dipped sheet and eaten with a dipping sauce. The lead (RecipeTin Eats) uses prawns and a peanut sauce made with hoisin; the vegetarian source fries tofu and glazes it with soy, oyster sauce and honey. Here the tofu is glazed with tamari and sugar, and the hoisin in the peanut sauce is replaced with tamari, sugar and rice vinegar so it stays vegan and gluten-free. Check the rice paper and vermicelli labels, which should list only rice and tapioca.
